Internal helper: make an offered modify = TRUE line run for a place

Source: R/utils.R
dot-jst_place_lines.Rd

modify = TRUE changes a data frame through its NAME, so jdeclare_missing(lst$d, ..., modify = TRUE) stops ("can only change a data frame that has a name"). Many builders paste the data argument as typed into such a line, and a call that named a place – jencode(lst$d, w, map = ...) – was offered lines that then stopped (the S343 item; Session 345). A place can be assigned to, so the line that runs for it is the assignment form, the one the durability reminder has given a place since Session 339: lst$d <- jdeclare_missing(lst$d, ...).

Usage

.jst_place_lines(lines)

Arguments

lines

Character vector: the physical lines of one message.

Value

Character vector of the same length.

Details

Done once, in the wrapper layer every emitter passes through, rather than at each of some forty builder sites: a printed call whose FIRST argument is a place and whose last is modify = TRUE always stops as printed, whichever function built it, so the rewrite needs to know nothing about the message it is in. A line is changed only when it is one whole call that parses, its first argument unnamed and a place by .jst_data_arg_kind(); every other line is returned untouched. The place is copied as typed, up to the first comma outside brackets and quotes. Only jdeclare_missing() and jconvert() take modify, and both return the data frame.
